extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of policy statements, official decrees, and reporting-level assertions appearing on a 1943 newspaper page covering international food-policy proposals, diplomatic broadcasts, official decrees, and human-interest profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plea for lowering or abolishing tariffs
rubrics_metrics.description: “A plea for lower or abolished tariffs … was placed before the United Nations Food Conference today by the Canadian delegation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Canadian memorandum urged tariff reduction/abolition as part of international cooperation; it framed tariff reduction as a necessary policy step to improve post-war trade and food distribution. (Context: presented alongside measures to maintain post-war employment and national income.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine tariff reduction with maintenance of employment and national income
rubrics_metrics.description: “The reduction or removal of protection in the form of tariff duties would not in itself suffice. Stable levels of employment and national income must be combined with the reduction of trade barriers.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance in the memorandum: tariff reductions alone are insufficient—economic stability (employment, national income) must accompany trade liberalization to achieve post‑war food and economic objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: International financing of buffer stocks of staple commodities
rubrics_metrics.description: Expression of approval for “internationally financed buffer stocks of staple commodities.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum and reporting endorsed earlier British suggestions for international buffer stocks, arguing that experience between the wars showed purely national approaches fail and that international treatment alone can adequately handle production and distribution problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assure the nutritional well‑being of every individual (state-supported food provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indorsement of suggestions that the post-war world ensure the nutritional well‑being of every individual; “there are few arguments in principle against efforts of the State, or of collaborating States, to provide additional quantities of food” for groups unable to maintain proper standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a policy standard: states or cooperating states should consider providing supplemental food to vulnerable groups as part of post‑war reconstruction and food security planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic initiative before expecting international aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Australia’s position that each country should use its own initiative to raise its economic standards and deal with food problems at home before expecting help from any international agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a cautionary principle for conference deliberations: national-level action and responsibility are prerequisites or complements to international assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of portraits/effigies/statues of living persons in official or public places
rubrics_metrics.description: Decree: “portraits of living persons, whether photographs, lithographs, portraits or statues, are prohibited in official or public places.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated purpose: “to avoid interpretations which too often cause trouble in spirit, military and civil.” Presented as an enforceable public-order rule in the new order; part of a broader cultural/political directive about public imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: French tricolored flag as the sole permitted emblem in official/public places
rubrics_metrics.description: Decree: “The sole emblem, the sole effigy, which under the new order will be permitted in official and public places will be the French tri‑colored flag, the lawful flag, without supplementary emblems.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: the tricolor is presented as the unifying emblem upon which all Frenchmen can agree and through which France will be presented in its proper appearance. This is an explicit restriction on other emblems in official/public contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for display of Allied flags despite portrait/emblem prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement: “This order, however, will not prevent the display of Allied flags.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies an exception to the prohibition on other emblems: displays of Allied flags remain permitted under the decree.
